# Uninvested published11 worker-storage fixture

This disposable observer creates one real published4.7.20002 or4.7.21002 save with empty `worker-robots-storage-4` work on every force. It writes only unrelated Base work to its named foreign force: current and queued Base research, saved Base progress, one disabled Base worker-speed row and the resulting Base worker-speed modifier. The player stays idle.

After its final source setter writes but before accepting or storing the source observation, the fixture emits one explicitly unaccepted public diagnostic frame. It records the foreign current/queue, `%.17g` actual and expected progress/saved fractions, the six setup rows, the independent modifier, supported research state, and that queue-enabled state is not declared by the2.0.77 runtime API. A diagnostic is not a source marker, save or acceptance result. Only those two research fractions admit a1e-7 representation tolerance; identities, levels, flags, counts, C4 emptiness and the modifier remain exact.

The fixture is removed for the middle published5.0.11 load. That selection is exactly Base plus MIR, so published11 itself performs its actual configuration callback without this observer, without a fresh11 initialization path and without any marker deletion or insertion. The controlled server-save creates the protected published11 input.

The same0.13.0 observer is newly added only with candidate17. Its configuration callback records the actual startup-setting Boolean and projected `mod_changes` rows after MIR runs, snapshots every valid force once by native index, and refuses unless canonical/default/head C4 rows are empty on every applicable force. It preserves every non-flag worker frame field exactly, while recording and validating the bounded native default-transfer flags: canonical disabled, the ordinary holder inheriting the source canonical flags and visibility, and the head gate disabled and hidden. It never reads MIR storage or writes worker state before that admission. The false setting route is the fixture-addition arm; the true setting route is explicitly a mixed startup-settings-plus-fixture-addition event, not startup-only admission evidence.

The identical archive is also passive for exact candidate16 added-mod negative arms. Its init, configuration and tick handlers return without fixture storage or world writes, allowing MIR16's own missing saved-route rejection to remain the native witness. An unexpected old16 success is adverse; this fixture does not turn it into an acceptance path.

After admission, only the player receives the actor's ordinary default-C4 lab work. Its seven prerequisite rows are an explicit authored set, checked against the public default-C4 contract and directly completed one by one; there is no recursive graph traversal. Before those writes, the actor captures the full public Base rows for `worker-robots-storage-2` and `worker-robots-storage-3`, including the candidate pre-configuration bonus. Their fixed Base effect vectors are each one `worker-robot-storage` modifier; after the writes, every non-researched field must be unchanged, each row must be researched, and the observed native storage-bonus delta must exactly equal the number of newly researched prefixes. This before/after receipt persists in the ordinary-started, saved and cold observations; it neither resets a bonus nor permits an arbitrary allowance. The ordinary C4 completion remains a separate one-step native effect from that post-prefix baseline. The full675-unit price uses the actual200-stack science-pack bound: each input refills only below64, records every accepted insert, and stops feeding once the native completion callback ends ordinary-active. The independently captured source row counts, flags and other untouched fields are preserved exactly across the transitions; they are captured source facts, not fixed absolute authored values for every native row. The foreign Base work and its independent native modifier must remain exact through the completion, save and two read-only cold processes. This fixture is not a Sage/Kal reproduction and does not establish private route-marker contents; the separate old16 negative is the native evidence that the same protected published11 source has no saved route.

Host controls validate actor boundaries and declared source/candidate tuples only. They do not build an archive, run Factorio or qualify the producer, candidate save, ordinary completion or cold reloads.
